findings.statement: Candidate domains, current action entity, turn owner and skill character have separate native fields; do not collapse their lifetimes.
Native entity ordering is a packed comparator, not AV + runtime ID. All-keys-equal sorting stability is unknown. Two prior summary details are corrected from saved instructions.

Native ordinary pick checks membership inputs, HasActionTurn and a conditional delay-lock filter; it can select before advancing remaining AV. AV zero alone is neither complete admission nor execution.
InsertAbilityPriority is a string-named config key; separate conditional override and global mapping declarations prevent treating raw source tokens as one global numeric sort.
WaitUse/InsertAbilityWorking/SelfDeathProcess/AllFinish declarations and separate pending/current/next accessors require visibility, running state and finished state to remain distinct.
Ordinary skill-execution completion is guarded; OnAfterSkillPerform is present on a path that returns false. TurnEnd is a separate FSM transition.

Reorder has an explicit event-driven path, TurnPrepare has an explicit sort/pick path, and Tick services queued Ultra work. A hybrid FSM/event/tick design is supported; immediate global selection after every mutation is not.
Source insertion/continuation requests can appear before their enclosing perform-finish marker. This supports request-versus-execution separation, not a proved nested execution or preemption point.
Actor relation must be distinct from candidate mechanism: special alias delay mutation and related-entity comparator-key inheritance exist, without a universal independent summon AV contract.
